remaining_concerns: The affected Spanish-language billing support segment remains below target and exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
There is no reviewed and approved risk-acceptance record covering that exposed segment; the available draft is incomplete and unsigned.
The policy threshold requires either exclusion of the affected use case or reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable.
Rollout limits, rollback, monitoring, and disclosure do not independently satisfy that policy predicate when exposure remains.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence. The response mainly narrows and caveats the original claim, and that clarification is useful, but it does not satisfy the governing policy. On the available record, the exposed Spanish-language billing support use case is still in scope for launch and there is still no reviewed risk acceptance covering that exposure. Under the stated policy, monitored rollout controls can mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or covered by reviewed risk acceptance. That required predicate remains unmet. The Actor's narrower framing may make the packet more accurate and less overstated, but it is not enough for compliant_with_caveats because the caveat here is itself an unresolved compliance condition, not merely a disclosure note.
